I recommend a two-piece enclosure with an open-top base, a separate lift-off lid, and board supports located from the board’s measured mounting holes. That makes the electronics accessible and lets us print the base with its opening upward. Lid retention, material, and cable relief depend on the electronics and use conditions.

What is the electronics’ maximum occupied envelope, including tall components and projecting connectors, in millimeters? Measure length and width viewed from above and height from the underside to the tallest component; a dimensioned sketch is ideal. If several boards are involved, measure their intended installed arrangement.

That envelope sets the cavity. While it is being measured, the design structure can be fixed: component envelope → proposed clearances → cavity → walls/base → board supports → cable openings → separate lid and retention. I’ll keep measured dimensions separate from proposed clearances; I have not created CAD or assumed a board size.

Use two editable parts, Base and Lid, with the base’s external lower-left-bottom as (0,0,0), x along the board’s 80 mm dimension, y along 50 mm, and z upward. All values below are synthetic supplied dimensions or direct calculations. This is a modeling plan; no CAD has been created.

Parameters and equations, in mm:

| Parameter | Value / relation |
|---|---|
| Board | 80 × 50 × 12 |
| Side gap | 2 on every side |
| Internal cavity | 84 × 54 |
| Side wall / base / lid | 2 / 2 / 2 |
| External footprint | 88 × 58 |
| Standoff height / OD | 3 / 6 |
| Board underside | z = 2 + 3 = 5 |
| Board top | z = 17 |
| Interior height above floor | 3 + 12 + 5 = 20 |
| Base top / lid underside | z = 22 |
| Lid top / total height | z = 24 |
| Board lower-left | (4,4,5) |
| Support centers | (7,7), (81,7), (81,51), (7,51) |
| Pilot holes | Ø2.5, blind 2 deep from standoff tops at z5 to z3 |
| Board holes | Ø3.2 at supplied board coordinates |
| Cable opening | Ø6 through right wall x = 88, centered (y,z) = (29,12) |

Feature order:

1. Base: fully define an 88 × 58 rectangle from the origin on an XY datum and extrude 22. Cut an 84 × 54 rectangle, offset 2 from each side, down 20 from the top. Expected floor z2 and four 2 mm walls. This explicit cut keeps wall and floor parameters independent.
2. Create four Ø6 circles on the floor at the support centers and boss-extrude 3 upward, merging into the floor. Add four Ø2.5 blind cuts 2 deep from their tops. The pilots end 1 mm above the floor top, with 3 mm material to the exterior underside.
3. On the right x-face, dimension the cable center from the external y0 and z0 datums, then cut Ø6 through the 2 mm side wall only. Use a bounded or up-to-next cut so it cannot cut the opposite wall.
4. Lid: separate 88 × 58 × 2 flat plate, placed with its underside at z22. The two external straps provide retention. Do not add screws, vents, snap fits, or a locating lip. Straps are assembly context unless their detailed geometry is requested; ensure their routes leave cable access clear.
5. Assemble the base and lid using stable datum references and inspect seating and removal access. Keep the board envelope and hole pattern as reference geometry for checking.

Check the 84 × 54 cavity, 2 mm side gaps, board z5–17, 5 mm roof gap, four support positions and pilot depths, 2 mm floor/walls/lid, and cable center and wall-only cut. The opening spans y26–32 and z9–15. Check cable/connector routing and bend space against the eventual hardware; the opening alone does not establish cable compatibility. Confirm one solid body in each part, fully defined production sketches, editable features, successful rebuild, and correct saved parts/configurations.

PETG FDM and base open-side up follow the preference; print the flat lid flat. Pilot sizing and 2 mm hardware engagement remain subject to the required fit trial. Print a pilot/fastener coupon before final assembly; process clearance is separate from the supplied nominal dimensions. Record physical fit separately from geometric checks.

The supplied long-edge dimensions conflict: 2 inches is 50.8 mm, while the note says 50 mm. The supplied short edge is 1 inch = 25.4 mm. I cannot inspect the unavailable photo, and an unscaled photo would not establish exact dimensions. Zero cable openings is a complete requirement, so I’ll keep the opening count at 0.

Which long-edge measurement should govern: 50.8 mm or 50 mm? Measure the board’s outside edges directly with calipers or a ruler, and retain the original inch note in the brief.

The useful draft can proceed with board_length = unresolved(50 or 50.8), board_width = 25.4 mm, board_height = unknown, mounting pattern = unknown, cable_opening_count = 0. Use a parameterized cavity, independent wall/base/lid parameters, and a separate removable lid. No dependent final footprint, support holes, or clearances can be committed yet; clearances can be proposed once the process and electronics envelope are known. No CAD or image-derived measurement is claimed.

Use a new part from your normal template and set display units to millimeters. No macro is needed.

1. Select an origin plane suited to the plate’s broad face, such as Top Plane or its localized equivalent, and start a sketch. Expected: an empty sketch on that plane.
2. Draw a center rectangle with its center coincident with the sketch origin. Keep adjacent sides horizontal and vertical. Add driving dimensions of 60 mm width and 30 mm height. Check the center, orientation and both sizes are constrained; inspect remaining degrees of freedom if the status still says under-defined. Colors can vary with settings.
3. Exit the sketch. Choose Boss-Extrude, Blind, depth 4 mm. Preview a single solid plate, then accept. Expected: one rectangular body with an editable sketch and extrusion feature.
4. Rebuild and use Measure or native dimensions to check 60 mm, 30 mm and 4 mm. Save under a new user-chosen .SLDPRT filename, then reopen and rebuild when feasible.

If the rectangle will not fully define or the extrusion preview differs, stop at that stage and describe the sketch status or preview. These are instructions; I have not inspected or saved your model.

With the exterior fixed at 100 × 70 mm, changing all four side walls from 2 to 3 mm makes the cavity 94 × 64 mm: 100 − 2×3 and 70 − 2×3. The board plus its required gaps needs 95 × 65 mm, so the revised cavity is short by 1 mm in each direction. The requested constraints conflict.

Revision record: side_wall 2 → 3 mm; exterior remains 100 × 70 mm; base and lid stay unchanged; cavity 96 × 66 → 94 × 64 mm; fit check changes from passing to failing. Do not silently enlarge the exterior or reduce the required gaps.

To preserve exterior and the 95 × 65 clearance envelope, each opposed wall pair can total at most 5 mm, meaning uniform walls at most 2.5 mm. Uniform 3 mm walls would require at least 101 × 71 mm exterior. Another route would require an explicitly approved change to the contents or required gaps, supported by actual fit evidence.

I recommend resolving this fit conflict before committing the dependent geometry. The change set for the brief, named wall/cavity equations, wall and cavity features, source constants, manual dimension steps, and acceptance checks must use the same final choice. Recheck board/support offsets, connectors, lid seating and any features referenced from inner walls; record base/lid as unchanged. Earlier 2 mm macro/manual/brief versions should be marked superseded only after that coordinated revision is prepared. No CAD or source file has been updated in this response.

I’d start with three separate editable parts—base, hinged arm and clamp—in an assembly. A hinge should retain one intended rotational degree of freedom during adjustment and lock for use; the clamp interface and load path should be finalized after the camera is selected. A bolted friction hinge is a possible starting choice; a toothed/indexed hinge trades continuous adjustment for more positive positioning. Neither has a rated capacity yet.

What camera or maximum camera envelope, mass, and attachment interface must it support? If the camera is undecided, those can remain explicit placeholders, but we should not finalize the clamp or claim a load rating.

Independent work can define an assembly datum at the base mounting plane, a hinge axis, separate base/arm/clamp parameters, and a motion-envelope study. The brief should retain base attachment, camera interface, mass/center of gravity, desired angle range, locking method, fastener access and manufacture as relevant unresolved requirements. Model the parts separately, assemble with appropriate mates preserving hinge rotation, then check travel, clamp clearance, interference and service access. Strength and holding performance need load analysis or physical trials once the camera and material are known.

A fully defined sketch has no remaining unconstrained degrees of freedom: its entities’ sizes and positions are fixed by dimensions and relations relative to the sketch’s references. For example, a rectangle needs its width, height, orientation and location constrained. It can still change when you edit its driving dimensions. Fully defined does not prove the design is correct; it means the sketch is constrained.

Make tomato-and-garlic pasta, a green salad and garlic bread for four.

Use 400–500 g dried pasta, one 800 g can crushed tomatoes, 3 garlic cloves, 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, pepper and basil; offer Parmesan at the table. Add a bag of salad leaves, a cucumber and a baguette.

Start the pasta water and heat the oven for the bread. Gently cook chopped garlic in oil for a minute, add tomatoes and simmer 15–20 minutes. Cook pasta until al dente, reserve a mug of cooking water, then toss with the sauce and enough pasta water to loosen it. Dress the salad just before serving. Allow about 30 minutes total.

Here is a provisional enclosure plan that can become concrete after measurement. I recommend an open-top base, four optional board-support locations driven from the eventual hole pattern, and a separate flat removable lid. This is a design proposal, not measured geometry or created CAD.

| Parameter | Provisional value / rule |
|---|---|
| Board length Bx, width By, maximum occupied height Bh | Unresolved; measure later |
| Board mounting coordinates / hole diameters | Unresolved; omit support holes until measured |
| Side gap g | Proposed 2 mm per side, subject to connectors and process |
| Wall t / base b / lid l | Proposed 2 / 2 / 2 mm starting geometry |
| Board underside support height s | Unresolved from underside components and fasteners |
| Top gap h | Proposed 5 mm starting allowance, subject to cabling/heat/access |
| Cavity | (Bx + 2g) × (By + 2g) × (s + Bh + h) |
| External footprint | (Bx + 2g + 2t) × (By + 2g + 2t) |
| Total closed height | b + s + Bh + h + l |
| Cable openings, ventilation and lid retention | Unresolved design requirements; do not turn these into zero |

Feature plan: fully dimension an outer base profile, extrude the base envelope, cut the inner cavity leaving the chosen floor, add supports from measured board datums, cut openings from measured connector/cable envelopes, then create the lid as a separate part and check assembly/removal access. Leave the board dimensions as symbolic parameters; an arbitrary numeric board size would hide the measurement dependency.

Use the board’s lower-left corner viewed above as the board datum, x along its length and y across its width; record z from the board underside. Later measure the complete occupied envelope including connectors, hole center coordinates and diameters, underside obstructions, and connector exit directions.
